newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip in thin trading.

text.p: Light institutional selling kept U.S. mortgage-backed securities just inside negative territory on a quiet Monday, traders said.

"We've been doing some light selling, taking some gains from bonds purchased earlier," one New York trader said. His firm unloaded mostly seasoned conventional 10-year paper and balloons, with an average life of about three years, he said.
Activity generally was very light. "It seems like it's holiday trading already," said one trader.
Thin retail participation in both Treasuries and mortgages resulted from lack of economic data, traders said.

Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were off 1/32 at 100-21/32, yielding 119 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. The 10-year Treasury note was down 2/32 at 102-07/32, yielding 6.20 percent.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper was off 1/32 as well, at 100-21/32 and 100-26/32, respectively.

A report on October housing starts set for Tuesday morning could prompt more of a market reaction. Economists in a Reuters poll on Friday projected starts increased to an annual rate of 1.443 million units last month from 1.438 million the month before.
